description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to enhance the connectivity, resilience, safety, and institutional sustainability of Iraq's priority road transport infrastructure and create jobs in transport and related sectors.

This project is in response to a request received from the GoI to support measures to enhance regional integration, advance domestic connectivity, optimize logistics synergies, and promote the operational and financial sustainability of the transport sector. The long-term framework for the operation entails to sequence investments in Expressway?No.?2, Ring Road?No.?4, improvised models for operating and maintaining (O&M) the road network, and developing logistics infrastructure into discrete, self standing phases, each contributing to the overarching program development objective of advancing the operational resilience, financial sustainability, and inter-modality of Iraq's transport sector to enhance national and regional connectivity.This project and its long-term framework will enable Iraq to embed systematic adaptation and learning, pilot and scale technical innovations, and progressively crowd in private financing. Early investments prioritized in this project, beginning with the “Baghdad - Samarra” segment, will serve as a live testbed for institutional reforms for private sector mobilization, initial implementation of PBC for M&O, and the development of a tolling strategy supported by the country's first ITS, with lessons directly shaping subsequent phases. This project will develop the first segment of Expressway No. 2 (i.e., Baghdad – Samarra). It will provide a proof-of-concept for operational and financial sustainability for the transport sector as well as linking to the existing Expressway No. 1, establishing a critical North–South corridor that connects domestic production hubs with regional markets. This project is designed to optimize multimodal and logistics synergies with the IREM initiative, while laying the institutional and policy foundations for long-term operational and financial sustainability. It also promotes sector resilience through adaptive learning and innovative financing and delivery mechanisms, including performance-based contracting (PBC), tolling strategies, Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS), and a PPP platform capable of mobilizing private investment backed by project-related guarantees.The Project is envisioned to include 4 components as follows:--Component 1: Resilient and Safe Road Infrastructure (US$835.15 million IBRD; US$41 million PCM)--Component 2: Support for Sector Reforms (US$ 10.6 million) This component will support institutional strengthening and reforms to enable the preparation and financing of Iraq's national road network. --Component 3: Implementation and Project Management Support (US$54.5 million) --Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response (US$0): Provision of immediate response to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, as needed.
